title: Meenakshi Thirukalyanam
body: King Malayadhwaja Pandya ruled Madurai (South India) and yearned for a successor. He performed a special ritual seated in front of a sacred fire (yagna) to appease The Gods and pray for a male child to succeed him. Out of this fire came a 3-year old divine girl who sat on his lap. A voice rang out of the heavens asking the king to train Her as his successor. He named her Princess Meenakshi (‘Meen’ meaning Fish, ‘Akshi’ meaning Eyes. Her beautiful eyes were said to be shaped like the contours of a fish) or Tadaatagai. The ‘Fish’ dances on the Pandya flag and Meenatchi may also mean ‘The Rule of The Fish’.
Malayadhwaja complied with the instructions from heaven and trained Her in the royal arts, politics and weaponry and She grew up as a warrior princess.

When She became old enough, he assembled princes and kings from far and wide so that she could pick a husband and rule Madurai together with Her husband. She demanded a husband who could defeat Her in battle which proved impossible. All the disappointed men went back to their kingdoms. She ascended the Pandya throne when her father passed and proceeded to conquer kingdoms around her. Her grace and strategy in battle was unrivaled and she continued her conquest in North India all the way up to Kailash (Abode of Lord Shiva – Himalayas in North India). She serves as an inspiration to all girls to stand up against gender norms and do what we enjoy.

She met Lord Shiva in full battle armor at the gates of Kailash. The warrior princess who hadn’t met her match in battle yet fell in love with the rugged, macho Lord Shiva even though His hair was matted, and He wore a tiger skin like an ascetic. He couldn’t shake Her beautiful face from His mind either. He requested her to return to Madurai and prepare for their wedding (Thirukalyanam). Once the royal wedding preparations were complete, Lord Shiva appeared all cleaned up as Sundareswarar (The Handsome One) in royal adornments to marry Queen Meenakshi for anything less would not be a match to her status. This is the only time in Hindu Mythology that Lord Shiva is depicted as a Householder (Grihastha) with normal attire. This is Lord Shiva we are talking about and He, Himself, changes his appearance for His beloved.

In weddings everywhere, the bride’s hand is placed in the groom’s hand to represent that the daughter of a family is becoming a part of another family. Please notice that Lord Sundareswarar’s hand is placed in Queen Meenakshi’s here symbolizing that He is being given away to Madurai where Queen Meenakshi continued Her rule. Lord Vishnu acts as Goddess Meenakshi’s Brother and pour sacred water on Their hands to signify the union.
This wedding is still enacted every year during Chithirai festival (April) in Madurai, the holy city ruled by Queen Meenakshi.
closing: For warrior princesses everywhere! Conquer Gender Norms!
